`is_valid_path` returns what `resolve` returns, the match, with `False` in place of the exception (`django/urls/base.py:resolve`, `django/urls/base.py:is_valid_path`).

It is the request's `path_info`, the path without the script prefix ([Making the request: `WSGIRequest` and `ASGIRequest`](../http/request.md)), with its percent escapes as the server left them, since neither the request nor the resolver decodes them (`django/core/handlers/wsgi.py:get_path_info`, `django/core/handlers/asgi.py:ASGIRequest.__init__`).

It is the request's `path_info`, the path without the script prefix ([Making the request: `WSGIRequest` and `ASGIRequest`](../http/request.md)), with its percent escapes as the server left them, since neither the request nor the resolver decodes them (`django/core/handlers/wsgi.py:get_path_info`, `django/core/handlers/asgi.py:ASGIRequest.__init__`).

Python's wsgiref server, on which Django's development server is built, decodes them into `"PATH_INFO"`, and from `"/files/maps/ground%20floor.pdf"` the museum's pattern for files captures `"maps/ground floor.pdf"`; behind a server that leaves the escape, it captures `"maps/ground%20floor.pdf"` (`django/core/servers/basehttp.py:WSGIRequestHandler.get_environ`).
The first entry to produce a match ends the search (`django/urls/resolvers.py:URLResolver.resolve`).

The root resolver, whose matcher captures nothing and which is given no extra arguments, adds none (`django/urls/resolvers.py:URLPattern.resolve`, `django/urls/resolvers.py:URLResolver.resolve`, `django/urls/resolvers.py:_get_cached_resolver`).

An extra argument given to `include` is not passed to each line of the included URLconf as if it had been written there, though the documentation calls the two forms "functionally identical" (`docs/topics/http/urls.txt`).
In the first case `ResolverMatch.extra_kwargs` still reports `{'room': 1}`, a value the view was not given (`django/urls/resolvers.py:URLResolver.resolve`).
Without an extra argument, `r"^a/([0-9]+)/"` over `r"^b/([0-9]+)/$"` gives `('1', '2')` for `"/a/1/b/2/"` (`django/urls/resolvers.py:URLResolver.resolve`).
A `ResolverMatch` carries the view and its arguments, which are what the handler needs, and besides them a record of how the match came about (`django/urls/resolvers.py:ResolverMatch.__init__`).

`BaseHandler.resolve_request` keeps the match on the request, as `HttpRequest.resolver_match`, where the middleware's `process_view` hooks and the view can read it, and a template through the request in its context (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.resolve_request`).
An entry that is a resolver whose list failed adds each chain it reported, with itself put at the front (`django/urls/resolvers.py:URLResolver._extend_tried`).

Outside the resolvers `"tried"` has one reader in Django, the debug page: under `settings.DEBUG`, `technical_404_response` shows each chain as a line, taking the list from the request's match when a view raised `Http404` after its path had matched ([The debug pages and `ExceptionReporter`](../views/debug.md#the-404-page)) (`django/views/debug.py:technical_404_response`).

Handed a 404 for a path without a final slash while `settings.APPEND_SLASH` is true, its method `CommonMiddleware.should_redirect_with_slash` asks `is_valid_path` about the path as it came and, when that fails, about the path with a slash; the second answer is the match itself, whose view the method reads for the mark `"should_append_slash"` that `no_append_slash` sets (`django/middleware/common.py:CommonMiddleware.should_redirect_with_slash`).

`CommonMiddleware.process_request` calls it only under `settings.PREPEND_WWW`, for a host that does not begin with `"www."`, and then answers with a redirect to the www. host before the handler has resolved anything; with that setting off, the default, `process_request` resolves nothing (`django/middleware/common.py:CommonMiddleware.process_request`).

The test client resolves each path it requested once more, lazily, to give a test `resolver_match` on the response ([The test client: `Client` and `ClientHandler`](../testing/client.md)) (`django/test/client.py:Client.request`).
